<a id="op-quitclientsession"></a>

### POST `/client/sessions/{id}/quit`

**End a client session as its client quits**

ADF Studio's quit (design daemon-backend.md §8.3). Ends the session like DELETE /client/sessions/{id}, then, with `stopDaemon: true`, stops the daemon only when this run was started by Studio (GET /version `startedBy: studio`); with other client sessions open the stop is pending until the last one ends or expires (they get `daemon_orphan_hold`). A daemon the CLI or a service started keeps running. When it stops, new sessions are refused before the answer is sent, so none can open between the decision and the stop. The answer and the daemon log give the reason. The shutdown is the daemon's own bounded one (the same as POST /daemon/shutdown), started after the answer. An unknown or expired session id is not an error (`ended: false`): the stop decision still applies. With `stopDaemon: true` the caller must be local (loopback, no proxy headers; the local proof behind a proxy), as for POST /daemon/shutdown.

Operation `quitClientSession` · bearer token

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string | yes | Client session id (POST /client/sessions) |

**Request body** (optional): [ClientQuitInput](#schema-clientquitinput)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stopDaemon` | boolean |  | Stop the daemon when allowed (Studio: `keepDaemonRunning` off). Default false: only the session ends. |

```json
{
  "stopDaemon": true
}
```

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [ClientQuitResult](#schema-clientquitresult) | The session ended; whether the daemon stops |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | stopDaemon is not a boolean |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | The request guard refused it: Host header not allowed (`host_not_allowed`, DNS-rebinding protection) or a browser cross-site request (`cross_origin`) |
| 405 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | This daemon has no client sessions |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "sessionId": "string",
  "ended": true,
  "stopping": true,
  "reason": "string",
  "otherSessions": 0
}
```

<a id="op-reloadclientcredentials"></a>

### POST `/client/reload-credentials`

**Re-read the credential stores a client changed**

ADF Studio moved credentials into or out of this daemon's stores while it ran (the mode-switch handover, design daemon-backend.md §11): ChatGPT and Grok sessions (auth.daemon.json), app-level MCP sign-ins and the `studio-runtime:<scope>` keychain entry. No secret crosses HTTP: the daemon re-reads the runtime identity entry (as GET /identity does), re-runs the credential unlock of every agent degraded on locked credentials, and brings loops that failed on a subscription's auth out of `error` for each subscription whose session is now in its store. Local callers only (loopback, no proxy headers; the local proof behind a proxy).

Operation `reloadClientCredentials` · bearer token

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [CredentialReloadResult](#schema-credentialreloadresult) | What the reload found |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | The request guard refused it: Host header not allowed (`host_not_allowed`, DNS-rebinding protection) or a browser cross-site request (`cross_origin`) |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "runtime": {
    "state": "adopted",
    "reason": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "unlocked": [
    {
      "agentId": "string",
      "filePath": "string"
    }
  ],
  "stillLocked": [
    {
      "agentId": "string",
      "filePath": "string"
    }
  ],
  "sessions": [
    "chatgpt"
  ],
  "recovered": 0
}
```

<a id="op-setclientsessionexitwhenclosed"></a>

### PUT `/client/sessions/{id}/exit-when-closed`

**Change a session's orphan behaviour**

The client's quit behaviour changed (ADF Studio's keepDaemonRunning): with `exitDaemonWhenClosed: true` the session's expiry stops a Studio-started daemon when no other session is open (the orphan rule, §8.3); with false it does not. Changing this setting requires a local caller (loopback, no proxy headers; local proof behind a proxy), returning 403 `loopback_only` otherwise.

Operation `setClientSessionExitWhenClosed` · bearer token

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string | yes | Client session id (POST /client/sessions) |

**Request body** (required): object

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exitDaemonWhenClosed` | boolean | yes |  |

```json
{
  "exitDaemonWhenClosed": true
}
```

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | object | Changed |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | exitDaemonWhenClosed is not a boolean |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | The request guard refused it: Host header not allowed (`host_not_allowed`, DNS-rebinding protection) or a browser cross-site request (`cross_origin`) |
| 404 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | No such client session |
| 405 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | This daemon has no client sessions |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "sessionId": "string",
  "exitDaemonWhenClosed": true
}
```

<a id="tag-remote-access"></a>

## Remote access

Other computers reach this daemon (docs/design/remote-access.md): the toggle, device tokens, pairing. Management routes answer this machine only: the install's token, a loopback caller without proxy headers, and the local proof (`X-ADF-Local-Proof`) in every mode; a device token gets 403 `device_token_refused`. `/remote/hello` and `/pair/*` need no token and answer 404 `remote_access_off` while remote access is off.

| Method | Path | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| GET | [`/remote-access`](#op-getremoteaccess) | Remote access status |
| PUT | [`/remote-access`](#op-updateremoteaccess) | Turn remote access on or off, rename |
| POST | [`/remote-access/networks`](#op-allowremotenetwork) | Allow on this network |
| DELETE | [`/remote-access/networks/{id}`](#op-forgetremotenetwork) | Remove an allowed network |
| POST | [`/remote-access/devices`](#op-createremotedevice) | Create a device token (copy-paste) |
| DELETE | [`/remote-access/devices/{id}`](#op-revokeremotedevice) | Revoke a device |
| POST | [`/remote-access/pairing`](#op-openpairing) | Open the pairing window |
| DELETE | [`/remote-access/pairing`](#op-closepairing) | Close the pairing window |
| POST | [`/remote-access/pairing/claims/{claimId}`](#op-decidepairingclaim) | Allow or deny a pairing request |
| POST | [`/remote-access/tailscale-serve`](#op-settailscaleserve) | Turn https through tailscale serve on or off |
| GET | [`/remote/hello`](#op-remotehello) | Who is this daemon (no token) |
| POST | [`/pair/claim`](#op-claimpairing) | Claim pairing with the host's code (no token) |
| GET | [`/pair/claims/{claimId}`](#op-pollpairingclaim) | Collect the result of a claim (no token) |

<a id="op-updateremoteaccess"></a>

### PUT `/remote-access`

**Turn remote access on or off, rename**

Live: no daemon restart. Turning on mints the daemon id (fingerprint); it listens only on networks the user allowed (POST /remote-access/networks). Turning off closes every remote listener, ends device sessions and connections, keeps the devices.

Operation `updateRemoteAccess` · bearer token

**Request body** (required): [RemoteAccessPatch](#schema-remoteaccesspatch)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean |  | On: opens listeners on private and Tailscale addresses (no daemon restart); off: closes them, ends device sessions and connections. Devices are kept. |
| `name` | string |  | The computer name other computers see: the runtime alias (settings runtimeAlias), else the host name |

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "string"
}
```

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|

| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Not this machine: a non-local caller or no local proof (`loopback_only`), a device token (`device_token_refused`), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 409 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | `env_bind`: ADF_DAEMON_HOST binds the daemon to the network itself |
| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

<a id="op-createremotedevice"></a>

### POST `/remote-access/devices`

**Create a device token (copy-paste)**

Mints a device token and returns it once; only its SHA-256 is stored (daemon-devices.json). The token is as powerful as the owner seed phrase.

Operation `createRemoteDevice` · bearer token

**Request body** (required): [RemoteDeviceInput](#schema-remotedeviceinput)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | yes |  |

```json
{
  "label": "string"
}
```

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | [RemoteDeviceCreated](#schema-remotedevicecreated) | The device and its token |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Bad label (`bad_request`) |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Not this machine: a non-local caller or no local proof (`loopback_only`), a device token (`device_token_refused`), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

Example 201 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "device": {
    "id": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "origin": "paired",
    "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "createdBy": "studio",
    "lastSeenAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "lastSeenAddress": "string",
    "connected": true,
    "connections": 0,
    "sessions": 0
  },
  "token": "string"
}
```

<a id="op-revokeremotedevice"></a>

### DELETE `/remote-access/devices/{id}`

**Revoke a device**

Removes the device (a 30-day tombstone answers its token with 401 `device_revoked`), ends its client sessions (their stream gets `session.ended` first) and destroys its connections, streams included.

Operation `revokeRemoteDevice` · bearer token

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string | yes | Device id |

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [RemoteDeviceRevoked](#schema-remotedevicerevoked) | The revoked device and what was closed |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Not this machine: a non-local caller or no local proof (`loopback_only`), a device token (`device_token_refused`), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 404 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Unknown device (`device_not_found`) |
| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "device": {
    "id": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "origin": "paired",
    "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "createdBy": "studio",
    "lastSeenAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "lastSeenAddress": "string",
    "connected": true,
    "connections": 0,
    "sessions": 0
  },
  "closedSessions": 0,
  "closedConnections": 0
}
```

<a id="op-openpairing"></a>

### POST `/remote-access/pairing`

**Open the pairing window**

A new 6-digit code for 120 s; replaces an open window. 5 wrong codes close it. The mDNS announcement shows `pair=1` while it is open.

Operation `openPairing` · bearer token

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | [PairingWindowView](#schema-pairingwindowview) | The window, with its code |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Not this machine: a non-local caller or no local proof (`loopback_only`), a device token (`device_token_refused`), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 409 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is off (`remote_access_off`) |
| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

Example 201 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "openedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "attemptsLeft": 0,
  "lockedSources": 0,
  "claim": {
    "claimId": "string",
    "deviceName": "string",
    "clientKind": "studio",
    "address": "string",
    "via": "lan",
    "tailnetLogin": "string",
    "at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

<a id="op-decidepairingclaim"></a>

### POST `/remote-access/pairing/claims/{claimId}`

**Allow or deny a pairing request**

The owner's answer after a correct code. Allow mints the device (origin `paired`) and keeps its token for the claimant's poll; the window closes either way.

Operation `decidePairingClaim` · bearer token

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claimId` | path | string | yes | Claim id (PairingClaimView) |

**Request body** (required): [PairingDecisionInput](#schema-pairingdecisioninput)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow` | boolean | yes |  |

```json
{
  "allow": true
}
```

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [PairingDecision](#schema-pairingdecision) | The decision |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | `allow` is not a boolean |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Not this machine: a non-local caller or no local proof (`loopback_only`), a device token (`device_token_refused`), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 404 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | No such pending claim (`claim_not_found`) |
| 409 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Already decided (`claim_decided`) |
| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "state": "approved",
  "device": {
    "id": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "origin": "paired",
    "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "createdBy": "studio",
    "lastSeenAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "lastSeenAddress": "string",
    "connected": true,
    "connections": 0,
    "sessions": 0
  }
}
```

<a id="op-settailscaleserve"></a>

### POST `/remote-access/tailscale-serve`

**Turn https through tailscale serve on or off**

Runs `tailscale serve --bg <port>` (on) or removes the https:443 entry when it forwards to this daemon (off). Clients call it only after the owner confirmed the command.

Operation `setTailscaleServe` · bearer token

**Request body** (required): [TailscaleServeInput](#schema-tailscaleserveinput)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes |  |

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [TailscaleServeResult](#schema-tailscaleserveresult) | Tailscale state and the command output |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | `enabled` is not a boolean |
| 401 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Missing or wrong bearer token (`unauthorized`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Not this machine: a non-local caller or no local proof (`loopback_only`), a device token (`device_token_refused`), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 502 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | The tailscale command failed (`tailscale_failed`, with `output` and `command`) |
| 503 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is not configured on this daemon (`unavailable`), or daemon-devices.json cannot be read (`devices_unreadable`) |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "tailscale": {
    "state": "absent",
    "serve": "on",
    "httpsUrl": "string",
    "serveCommand": "string"
  },
  "output": "string"
}
```

<a id="op-remotehello"></a>

### GET `/remote/hello`

**Who is this daemon (no token)**

The mDNS announcement's content, for clients that cannot hear mDNS (tailnet peers, a typed address). No secret. 30 per minute per source address.

Operation `remoteHello` · no authentication

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [RemoteHello](#schema-remotehello) | Name, fingerprint, pairing open |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | The request guard refused it: Host header not allowed (`host_not_allowed`, DNS-rebinding protection) or a browser cross-site request (`cross_origin`) |
| 404 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Remote access is off (`remote_access_off`) |
| 429 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Rate limited (`rate_limited`, Retry-After) |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "name": "string",
  "fingerprint": "string",
  "pairingOpen": true,
  "clientApiVersion": 0
}
```

<a id="op-claimpairing"></a>

### POST `/pair/claim`

**Claim pairing with the host's code (no token)**

A correct code puts the claim before the owner (202); the token comes only after the owner allows it (GET /pair/claims/{claimId}, with the collect secret). Wrong codes are answered after 1 s; 5 from one source lock that source out of the window (429 until it closes, the owner is told), 20 in total close it. Per source: one claim per 2 s, 10 per 10 minutes. A source is the socket address (forwarded headers are never read), or the tailnet user behind tailscale serve.

Operation `claimPairing` · no authentication

**Request body** (required): [PairClaimRequest](#schema-pairclaimrequest)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes |  |
| `deviceName` | string | yes | Becomes the device label; control and bidi characters are refused |
| `clientKind` | `"studio"` \| `"cli"` | yes |  |

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "deviceName": "string",
  "clientKind": "studio"
}
```

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 202 | [PairClaimAccepted](#schema-pairclaimaccepted) | Waiting for the owner |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Bad code, device name or client kind (`bad_request`) |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Wrong code (`wrong_code`, with `attemptsLeft`: for this source and the window together), or the request guard (`host_not_allowed`, `cross_origin`) |
| 404 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | No open window (`pairing_closed`) or remote access is off (`remote_access_off`) |
| 409 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Another claim waits for the owner (`pairing_busy`) |
| 429 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Rate limited, or this source is locked out of the window after 5 wrong codes (`rate_limited`, Retry-After) |

Example 202 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "claimId": "string",
  "expiresAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "collectSecret": "string"
}
```

<a id="op-pollpairingclaim"></a>

### GET `/pair/claims/{claimId}`

**Collect the result of a claim (no token)**

Long poll: waits up to `wait` seconds while pending. Needs the claim's collect secret (`X-ADF-Pair-Secret`); the claim id alone collects nothing. An approved result (with the device token) is delivered once, then the claim is gone (404). `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Operation `pollPairingClaim` · no authentication

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claimId` | path | string | yes | Claim id (POST /pair/claim) |
| `wait` | query | integer |  |  |
| `X-ADF-Pair-Secret` | header | string | yes | The claim's collectSecret (POST /pair/claim). Compared in constant time; a missing or wrong one answers 404 `claim_not_found`, as an unknown claim does |

**Responses**

| Status | Body | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | [PairClaimResult](#schema-pairclaimresult) | pending, denied, or approved with the token |
| 400 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | `wait` out of range |
| 403 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | The request guard refused it: Host header not allowed (`host_not_allowed`, DNS-rebinding protection) or a browser cross-site request (`cross_origin`) |
| 404 | [ErrorResponse](#schema-errorresponse) | Unknown, expired or collected claim, or a missing or wrong collect secret (`claim_not_found`), or remote access is off (`remote_access_off`) |

Example 200 (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "state": "pending"
}
```

<a id="schema-chatbody"></a>

### ChatBody

`text`, or `content` (content blocks, which win when both are given).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string |  |  |
| `content` | object[] |  | The message as content blocks (Studio's AGENT_INVOKE `content`): `text`, `image_url` ({url}: a data URI), `input_audio` ({data, format}), `video_url` ({url}). Body limit 128 MiB. |
| `content[].type` | `"text"` \| `"image_url"` \| `"input_audio"` \| `"video_url"` | yes |  |
| `loop` | string |  | Cognition loop to talk to; absent = main. Unknown loop: 404; disabled loop: 409. |
| `echoed` | boolean |  | `true`: the sending client session (`X-ADF-Client-Session`) already shows the message (Studio's AGENT_INVOKE), so that session's stream skips the turn's `trigger_message`. Every other client still gets it. Without the header it has no effect. |

<a id="schema-createagentbody"></a>

### CreateAgentBody

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | File name (<= 64 chars). Omitted: a generated adjective-plant name. |
| `directory` | string |  | Absolute, existing directory. Default: settings.agentsFolder, else ~/Documents/adf-agents. |
| `template` | string |  | Template id (GET /templates). Default: settings.defaultTemplateId, else `standard`. |
| `provider` | string |  | App provider id (must exist in settings.providers) |
| `model` | string |  |  |
| `start` | boolean |  | Default `false`. |
| `identityDraftId` | string |  | An identity draft (POST /identity/drafts): the new agent gets its DID. Consumed; an unknown or expired draft falls back to a fresh identity, reported in `identityDraft` and `warnings`. |
| `load` | boolean |  | false: create the file and load nothing (Studio's FILE_CREATE, MESH_FOUND_AGENT). With `holder`, the file is held as an open document. Default `true`. |
| `replace` | boolean |  | true: a file of that name exists and the user chose to replace it (Studio's save dialog asked): the new agent is written over it. Refused (409 `name_taken`) while that file runs or is open. Without the owner identity the agent is still made, its identity not sealed to an owner; `warnings` says so. Default `false`. |

|---|---|---|---|

<a id="schema-daemonversioninfo"></a>

### DaemonVersionInfo

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes | Build version (package version; `dev` when run from sources outside npm) |
| `clientApiVersion` | integer | yes | Version of the internal client API (`/client/*` and its frames). 2 since executor frames carry turn ids and the `turn` frame exists. ADF Studio needs exactly its own number; the terminal app reads 1 and 2. |
| `settingsPath` | string \| null | yes | Settings file this daemon reads and writes; null for an in-memory store |
| `dataDir` | string \| null | yes | Directory of the settings file: access token, pid file, logs, runtime keys |
| `runtimeId` | string \| null | yes | Mesh runtime id from settings; null until one was minted |
| `pid` | integer | yes | Daemon process id |
| `startedBy` | `"studio"` \| `"cli"` \| `"service"` | yes | Who launched this daemon run (`ADF_DAEMON_STARTED_BY`) |
| `trust` | [DaemonTrustStatus](#schema-daemontruststatus) |  |  |
| `localProof` | object |  | Whether this run has a local proof (X-ADF-Local-Proof). Without one, every route that needs it refuses (POST /identity/import, the stored-value reveal routes); on Windows that happens when icacls cannot restrict the proof file. Absent in daemons before this field. |
| `localProof.available` | boolean | yes |  |
| `localProof.problem` | string \| null | yes | Why there is no proof; null when available. |
| `keychainProblem` | string \| null |  | Set when this machine has an OS keychain (Windows, macOS) that the daemon could not read at start (three tries over 5 s), so it runs on its passphrase file: why, and what to do (restart the daemon once the keychain works). Owner create, restore, import and trust-daemon answer 409 `keychain_unavailable` meanwhile. Null otherwise; absent without an owner identity service or in older daemons. |

<a id="schema-daemonruntimeadoption"></a>

### DaemonRuntimeAdoption

Whose runtime identity the daemon uses. `adopted`: ADF Studio's, from a verified OS keychain entry for this settings file. `absent`: no such entry. `rejected`: an entry exists but failed verification (`reason`). `unavailable`: no usable OS keychain. In every state but `adopted` the daemon runs as its own runtime, and Studio-made agents' credentials unlock through the trusted-daemon key `daemonEncPublicKey`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | `"adopted"` \| `"absent"` \| `"rejected"` \| `"unavailable"` | yes |  |
| `source` | `"studio"` \| `"daemon"` | yes |  |
| `reason` | `"malformed"` \| `"unsupported_version"` \| `"no_owner"` \| `"owner_mismatch"` \| `"bad_signing_key"` \| `"subject_mismatch"` \| `"bad_delegation"` \| `"runtime_did_mismatch"` \| `"enc_key_mismatch"` \| `"scope_mismatch"` \| `null` | yes |  |
| `daemonRuntimeDid` | string \| null | yes | The daemon's own runtime DID |
| `daemonEncPublicKey` | string \| null | yes | Base64 raw X25519 public key of the daemon's runtime-enc-key (what Studio lists in trustedDaemonEncKeys) |
| `message` | string | yes | One sentence for the UI |

| `switchOwner` | boolean |  | Required (true) when the phrase belongs to another owner than this machine's |

<a id="schema-agentpowerstat"></a>

### AgentPowerStat

Reach, Access or Autonomy: a capped level on a 1-20 scale. fill = clamp(points / max, 0, 1); level = 1 + round(19 * fill), so an empty config is Lv 1 and a maxed-out one Lv 20. `max` is the sum of every capped positive factor of the stat (counts such as MCP servers and chat adapters only count their heaviest few). Gated points count toward the level. `points` is `open` + `gated`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | integer | yes |  |
| `points` | number | yes | Points behind the level, after mitigations |
| `max` | number | yes | Points of a maxed-out config for this stat |
| `fill` | number | yes | points / max, clamped: how much of the possible power the agent has |
| `open` | number | yes | Points whose capability runs without approval (mitigations come off these first) |
| `gated` | number | yes | Points whose capability needs approval |
| `high` | boolean | yes | True when open / max >= 0.6 (open level 12 or more): much of this runs without anyone asking |
| `rawPoints` | number | yes | Sum of factor points, mitigations included |
| `factors` | [AgentStatFactor](#schema-agentstatfactor)[] | yes |  |

<a id="schema-agentstatfactor"></a>

### AgentStatFactor

One line of a stat breakdown.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Stable id, e.g. `tool:compute_exec`, `mcp:github`, `visibility` |
| `label` | string | yes |  |
| `points` | number | yes | Points this factor adds; negative for mitigations; 0 for an item past its kind's cap (7th MCP server, 4th chat adapter), listed but not counted |
| `gated` | boolean | yes | True when the capability needs human approval |
| `configPath` | string | yes | Config path (or table) that controls this factor |

<a id="schema-agentexperiencestat"></a>

### AgentExperienceStat

Experience. xpForLevel(L) = 5 * (L - 1)^2.25; level = largest L with xpForLevel(L) <= score.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | integer | yes |  |
| `progress` | number | yes | Progress within the current level |
| `score` | number | yes | Total XP (sum of signal XP) |
| `levelStart` | number | yes | XP at which the current level starts |
| `nextLevelAt` | number | yes | XP at which the next level starts |
| `breakdown` | object[] | yes |  |
| `breakdown[].id` | `"contextsWorked"` \| `"memoryTokens"` \| `"skills"` \| `"localTables"` \| `"localRows"` \| `"filesWritten"` \| `"agentsSpawned"` \| `"messages"` \| `"ageDays"` | yes |  |
| `breakdown[].label` | string | yes |  |
| `breakdown[].value` | number | yes | Raw count |
| `breakdown[].xp` | number | yes | XP this signal adds |
| `nextLevel` | object | yes | What one more level takes (xp = nextLevelAt - score), in units of the cheapest signals |
| `nextLevel.xp` | number | yes |  |
| `nextLevel.contexts` | integer | yes | Contexts of work worth the remaining XP |
| `nextLevel.memoryTokens` | integer | yes | Memory tokens worth the remaining XP |
| `nextLevel.skills` | integer | yes | Skills worth the remaining XP |
| `nextLevel.hint` | string | yes |  |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `localRows` | integer | yes | Rows across `local_*` tables (the first 50 by name) |

| `agentsSpawned` | integer \| null | yes | Tracked agents whose adf_parent_did names this agent; null when no fleet scan has run |
| `messages` | integer | yes | Loop messages ever written, every loop current and past (adf_loop's shared AUTOINCREMENT high-water mark; compaction, clears and loop deletion do not lower it) |

<a id="schema-agentupcomingwake"></a>

### AgentUpcomingWake

One timer due soon, as raw pieces. `system` timers carry `lambda` and `input`; `agent` timers carry `loop` and `prompt`. Both texts are the timer payload as stored, cut to 1000 characters (ending in an ellipsis).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `at` | number | yes | next_wake_at (ms epoch) |
| `scope` | `"system"` \| `"agent"` | yes | `system` runs a lambda; `agent` wakes a loop |
| `lambda` | string |  | system: lambda reference, e.g. `lib/sync.ts:run` |
| `input` | string |  | system: payload passed to the lambda |
| `loop` | string |  | agent: loop the wake dispatches to (`main` when the timer names none) |
| `prompt` | string |  | agent: payload the loop wakes with |

| `exitDaemonWhenClosed` | boolean |  | Stop a Studio-started daemon when this session expires and no other session is open. Default false. |
| `umbilical` | boolean |  | Also stream the umbilical envelopes GET /events carries, as `umbilical` frames, without `turn.delta` (the focused agent's tokens arrive as executor frames). The terminal app sets it. Default false. |
| `pid` | integer |  | The client's process id, kept only from a caller on this machine (local proof). A new session of the same client ends that client's sessions whose pid is no longer running and whose stream is closed (a relaunch after a crash), without the orphan rule. |

### ClientStreamGap

Data of the `stream.gap` control frame on a client session stream: frames were lost; reload state.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `reason` | `"evicted"` \| `"epoch_changed"` \| `"oversized"` | yes | `evicted`: frames after `requestedCursor` were dropped before they were written (slow reader, long disconnect). `epoch_changed`: the cursor is from another session; the whole ring follows. `oversized`: one frame was larger than the 4 Mi-character frame limit and was not kept (this session only). |
| `epoch` | string | yes |  |
| `requestedCursor` | integer \| null | yes |  |
| `oldestCursor` | integer \| null | yes |  |
| `latestCursor` | integer | yes |  |
| `dropped` | integer |  | Frames lost (`evicted`, `oversized`) |
| `size` | integer |  | Serialized size of the oversized frame |

<a id="schema-clientframe"></a>

### ClientFrame

One client-session frame. `executor`: `{agentId, filePath, loop?, event, stripped?, turnId?, absorbedTurnIds?}` with `event` a raw executor event `{type, payload, timestamp, loop?}`. `turn`: `{agentId, filePath, loop?, outcome: discarded, turnIds, unansweredTurnIds}`, to every session. `host`: `{agentId, filePath, type, payload, timestamp}`. `umbilical` (sessions opened with `umbilical: true`): `{agentId, event}` with `event` the envelope GET /events carries; never `turn.delta`. `push`: `{topic, agentId, filePath, payload}`; topics: daemon_orphan_hold, config_changed, inbox, workspace_data, approvals, mesh, inter_agent_message, templates, tracked_dirs, file_renamed, agent_path_changed, autostart, autostart_overflow, adf_file_created, mcp_install, adapter_install, sandbox_install, mcp_status, adapter_status, compute_phase, browser_session (payloads: src/main/daemon/client-sessions.ts ClientPushPayloads). JSON rules: a key whose value is undefined is omitted (treat missing as undefined), BigInt becomes its decimal string, a reference cycle becomes "[Circular]". A session not focused on an agent gets that agent's executor frames of the background whitelist (state_changed, ask_request, tool_approval_request, response_metadata, error, turn_complete, adf_file_created) in full, `tool_call_start` with its input fields cut to 2048 characters, `tool_call_result` stripped, every other type as a stub; `inbox` and `inter_agent_message` pushes arrive as stubs (counts; no content).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | integer | yes | Resume cursor, per session |
| `kind` | `"executor"` \| `"host"` \| `"push"` \| `"umbilical"` \| `"turn"` | yes |  |
| `turnId` | string |  | `executor`: the turn the event belongs to (the `turnId` POST …/chat answered); absent outside a turn. |
| `absorbedTurnIds` | string[] |  | `executor` `turn_complete` (not interrupted) and `error`: the other chats this turn answered; they end with it. |
| `outcome` | `"discarded"` |  | `turn`: a stop or `off` dropped queued chats (`turnIds`) and cut off the turn answering `unansweredTurnIds`. |
| `turnIds` | string[] |  |  |
| `unansweredTurnIds` | string[] |  |  |
| `agentId` | string \| null |  |  |
| `filePath` | string \| null |  |  |
| `loop` | string |  |  |
| `event` | object |  |  |
| `stripped` | `"tool_result"` \| `"tool_input"` \| `"stub"` |  | Reduced for a session not focused on the agent: `tool_result` (result content dropped, `resultSize` added), `tool_input` (`tool_call_start` with each input field cut to 2048 characters, `inputTruncated: true`), `stub` (only short scalar fields plus `size`). |
| `type` | string |  |  |
| `topic` | string |  |  |
| `payload` | any |  |  |
| `timestamp` | number |  |  |
| `unserializable` | `true` |  | The payload could not be serialized; it is `{unserializable: reason}`. |
